scores.evidence: The decision flowchart s4-sort uses a top-down layout with Japanese labels that stay readable at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-18.png) and has a caption (図1). The definition tables (s1-defs, s4-defs) turn into stacked cards on mobile, and the code blocks s3-code and p-model-code wrap without cutting anything off (pages/mobile-jp-13.png, pages/mobile-jp-29.png).

Each segment follows the same pattern: a definition card, then a short list or prompt, then an inline check, so no long plain-text runs appear in the full-length PNGs. Only mobile screen 4 counts as text-only, and it holds the end of the s1-defs table plus the s1-pick list (pages/mobile-jp-04.png).

All screens are in Japanese, including the diagram labels, step titles and quiz options, with English terms in parentheses on first use. Text contrast is good, inline code chips stay whole, and on every mobile screen the answer and copy buttons sit clear of the top and bottom bars.

niceToHave: p-model-code: at 390 px, line 5 `test('4で割り切れる年はうるう年', () => {` wraps and leaves a single `{` on its own line, while lines 9 and 13 fit (pages/mobile-jp-29.png). A slightly shorter test name, such as '4の倍数はうるう年', would keep the four tests visually parallel. The same happens in s3-code lines 5 and 13 (pages/mobile-jp-13.png).

s3-prompt-write / s3-prompt-green / p-prompt-write: the prompt bodies show literal backticks around identifiers (`isPostalCode`, `postal.mjs`). This is correct for copy-paste but looks noisy when read. Consider dropping the backticks where the name is unambiguous (pages/mobile-jp-12.png, pages/desktop-jp-08.png).

summary: No hard failures in metrics.json (no horizontal overflow, console or mermaid errors, unknown blocks or broken images), and no personal data on any of the 25 desktop or 38 mobile screens. The flowchart, definition cards, step lists, code blocks and the six-question exam all read cleanly at 390 px and 1440 px. The only remaining polish is optional: shorter test names in the code samples so no line wraps to a lone brace on mobile.
